projects.title: GreenLLM
projects.description: An intelligent carbon-aware LLM routing and management system built in 2 weeks as part of the SMART capstone project.
projects.fullDescription:
In just 2 weeks, we built an intelligent carbon-aware LLM routing and management system as part of the SMART capstone project during our 4th year in the Computer Science engineering program at INSA Lyon. We placed 2nd and are proud of what we built: GreenLLM.

This project didn't come out of nowhere. About 3 months prior, during the AGIR program — an initiative focused on developing high-impact, interdisciplinary projects for society — we collaborated with Wavestone on a concrete industry challenge: how can we estimate the carbon impact of AI systems? We developed a first methodology to approach this problem, and that work sparked something bigger.

Building on that foundation, we explored how such insights could directly inform how AI systems are used in practice. That's how GreenLLM emerged: a system designed to intelligently route and manage LLM usage, with efficiency and environmental impact in mind.

This is just the beginning. We're continuing to explore where this can go.

projects.title: Hotel Juan María Website
projects.description: Redesign and development of the official website and brand identity for Hotel Juan María in Tuluá.
projects.fullDescription: This project involves the full redesign and development of the website for Hotel Juan María, a local hospitality business based in Tuluá, Colombia. As lead frontend developer, I built the site using Next.js and integrated a headless CMS to allow easy content management by hotel staff. The site is designed to be modern, responsive, and user-friendly, highlighting the hotel's services, rooms, and booking options. In addition to the development, we also led the redesign of the hotel's visual identity, including a new logo. While still in development, the platform aims to increase the hotel's online visibility and improve the guest experience through digital transformation.

projects.title: Early To Wear
projects.description: A fashion discovery platform that redefines how Colombians discover and buy emerging fashion brands.
projects.fullDescription:
Early To Wear was a fashion discovery web platform created to empower independent fashion brands and revolutionize how Colombians found, followed, and bought from them. The app addressed the lack of visibility and access for local fashion startups, offering an intuitive shopping experience tailored to user preferences. With features like curated collections, advanced style filtering, sustainable and second-hand categories, and smart recommendations, ETW helped users discover fashion that truly fit their identity—before anyone else.

Although the platform is no longer live, the project successfully onboarded 6 emerging brands and provided us with invaluable insights into digital product design, community building, and brand acquisition strategies. Early To Wear was developed as part of the Universidad de los Andes Innovation Week 2024 and represented a hands-on exploration of how technology can empower creative industries in Latin America.
projects.client: Universidad de los Andes – Innovation Week 2024

projects.title: UniMarket
projects.description: A peer-to-peer campus marketplace for buying, selling, and trading academic resources.
projects.fullDescription:
UniMarket is a student-driven marketplace designed to streamline the buying, selling, and trading of academic resources among university students. The platform solves the inefficiencies of social media groups by providing a secure, course-filtered, and verified transaction system. It incorporates features such as wishlist notifications, ask & offer dynamics, real-time chat, transaction tracking, smart filtering by major or course, and a multi-stream revenue model including sponsored listings and premium features.

UniMarket also integrates Augmented Reality (AR) tools to help users measure product sizes before purchase, and includes AI-powered recommendations and context-aware features such as QR-based transaction confirmation that only succeeds when both devices are within Bluetooth range—ensuring physical presence and preventing fraud.

Designed for students, by students—UniMarket promotes cost-efficiency, sustainability, and trust on campus.
projects.client: Universidad de los Andes – Mobile Development Course

projects.title: Pawsitivity DogSpa
projects.description: A full-stack pet spa platform with booking, packages, and playful visuals.
projects.fullDescription: Pawsitivity DogSpa is a web application designed to bring joy and convenience to pet owners by offering a seamless digital experience for booking spa services, exploring service packages, filtering locations, and browsing pet products. The platform features real-time package filtering by branch, interactive reservation management, and dynamic service previews with random dog images using DogAPI. Built with a user-centered design, the project emphasizes clarity, accessibility, and a touch of fun through canine-themed elements.

projects.title: Traffic Analysis
projects.description: Real-time traffic monitoring along Bogotá's Carrera 7 using computer vision to extract congestion levels from map imagery and validate with routing metrics.
projects.fullDescription:
This project analyzes real-time traffic on Carrera 7 in Bogotá by combining computer vision with geodata and Python automation. The goal was to pull the traffic layer from Google Maps, extract congestion levels visually (instead of paying for the Traffic API), and compare those results with precise routing estimates like speed, distance, and travel times. 
 
 The pipeline works by grabbing the traffic map for each segment, using computer vision to read the congestion colors, running optional routing queries for validation, and then visualizing everything through interactive maps and charts. 
 
 The biggest challenge was making a CV system that could reliably read the traffic level from color patterns while keeping segment-by-segment consistency. And beyond the technical work, there was also the economic challenge: getting live traffic data from Google's API is extremely expensive if you query it continuously...  So the goal was to build a system that didn't rely on expensive API calls, could run automatically every hour or every few minutes, and still gave high-quality traffic estimations. 
 
 The solution? 
 I developed a Python pipeline that processes each segment of Carrera 7 and extracts its traffic level visually, directly from the traffic map. This avoids the need to call Google's paid Traffic API, which charges per request. And even though the system wasn't ultimately deployed, the solution I delivered was fully functional and ready to run in the cloud. Here's the key point though, to monitor the 10 segments every minute, the Google Traffic Advanced API would require: 10 segments × 1,440 calls per day × 31 days = 446,400 API calls per month. Google charges about $10 per 1,000 calls, so this would cost: $4,464/month. But my approach didn't make those paid traffic requests. It simply loaded the traffic layer visually, which is: 
  basically free with Google's $200/month credit 
  or only a few cents if you exceed it 
  and easy to cache 
 So instead of paying €4,000 a month, the system would run for almost nothing. 
 
The approach showed that it's possible to monitor a major urban corridor in real time without paying thousands of euros in API costs, thanks to a computer-vision workaround. This way, even small cities can afford to monitor and learn more from data on their most crowded highways.
projects.client: Academic / Research Project – Universidad de Los Andes
